summary:
TerraMotion is an interactive application developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 challenge, “Dancing with the SARs.” It uses NASA–ISRO NISAR satellite observations to explore surface changes across the Svartsengi–Sundhnúkur volcanic system on Iceland’s Reykjanes Peninsula.

The application brings together three NISAR data products: GUNW interferometric measurements, GOFF radar pixel offsets, and GCOV radar backscatter observations. It also incorporates independent GNSS measurements to compare satellite observations with ground-based geodetic data.

Through interactive maps, temporal comparisons, visualisations, and scientific quality assessments, TerraMotion makes complex SAR observations more accessible and interpretable. Its scientific governance section documents uncertainty, data limitations, and unresolved discrepancies rather than presenting every observed change as confirmed ground displacement.

The project aims to demonstrate how multi-product satellite observations and independent geodetic measurements can support transparent exploration of volcanic surface dynamics.
details:
TerraMotion is an interactive application developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. It uses NASA–ISRO NISAR satellite observations to explore surface changes across the Svartsengi–Sundhnúkur volcanic system on Iceland's Reykjanes Peninsula.

The application combines three NISAR data products:

• GUNW: examines relative line-of-sight ground displacement through interferometric measurements.
• GOFF: analyses radar image pixel offsets between acquisitions.
• GCOV: examines changes in radar backscatter response.

It also incorporates independent GNSS observations to compare satellite measurements with ground-based geodetic data.

Built using Python, Streamlit, NumPy, scientific processing libraries and visualisation tools, TerraMotion provides interactive maps, temporal comparisons, quality assessments and a dedicated scientific limitations section.

Its objective is to make satellite-based volcanic deformation analysis more accessible, transparent and understandable.

The project prioritises scientific caution. Measurements are relative and subject to uncertainty. Backscatter changes are not direct displacement measurements, and unresolved differences between InSAR and GNSS observations are documented rather than concealed.

Super Intelligence tools, including ChatGPT and Google Antigravity, assisted with programming, debugging, research organisation, documentation and presentation preparation. Scientific interpretation and project decisions were reviewed by the team.
